steps.title: Plate 293T cells
steps.instruction: Seed 293T cells into a 6‑well plate adding 2 mL of 293T cell culture medium per well so that cells reach 70–90 % confluence on the day of transfection.

steps.title: Prepare transfection reagents
steps.instruction: Make the three solutions required for Lipofectamine 3000 transfection:

substeps.instruction: Lipofectamine 3000 solution: mix 7.5 µL Lipofectamine 3000 with 125 µL Opti‑MEM (total 132.5 µL). Vortex 2–3 s.
Plasmid DNA with P3000: dilute 2.5 µg pCAG‑GFP1 POD‑nAb‑WPRE (1 µg/µL) in 125 µL Opti‑MEM, add 5 µL P3000 (2 µL per µg DNA). Mix by pipetting.
DNA‑lipid complex: combine 125 µL of the Lipofectamine 3000 solution (50 %) with 125 µL of the DNA‑P3000 solution (50 %). Tap to mix and incubate 10–15 min at 20–25 °C.

steps.title: Transfect 293T cells
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL of the DNA‑lipid complex to each well containing the 293T cells.

steps.title: Incubate transfected cells
steps.instruction: Culture the cells for 3 days at 37 °C in a 5 % CO₂, 95 % humidity incubator.

steps.title: Harvest POD‑nAb supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect the culture supernatant into a 50 mL conical tube, centrifuge at 3,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, filter through a 0.22 µm syringe filter, add thimerosal 10 % stock to a final concentration of 0.05 % (2.4 µL per 1,200 µL), and store at 4 °C (stable ≤6 months).

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse for AAV injection
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia in an adult mouse (8–16 weeks) by isoflurane inhalation.

steps.title: Inject AAV vector
steps.instruction: Using a 30‑G insulin syringe, inject 100 µL of AAV2/PHP.eB CAG‑EGFP‑WPRE (5 × 10¹⁰ gc/mL) into the retro‑orbital sinus.

steps.title: Post‑injection recovery
steps.instruction: Return the mouse to its home cage with food and water ad libitum; house under specific‑pathogen‑free conditions for 3–4 weeks, monitoring health twice weekly.

steps.title: Prepare solutions for perfusion
steps.instruction: Filter PBS and the 4 % PFA fixative solution through filter paper and keep on ice.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse for perfusion
steps.instruction: Inject sodium pentobarbital (50 mg/mL) intraperitoneally at 200 mg/kg; confirm depth of anesthesia by lack of eye‑blink and toe‑pinch reflexes.

steps.title: Perfuse mouse
steps.instruction: Open the thoracic cavity, cut the right atrial appendage, insert a 23‑G needle into the left ventricle, and perfuse sequentially:

substeps.instruction: 20 mL ice‑cold fixative (4 % PFA in PBS) over 2–3 min.

steps.title: Post‑fix brain
steps.instruction: Excise the brain, place it in 12 mL fixative solution in a 15 mL conical tube, and gently shake at 50–100 rpm for 24 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Embed brain in agar
steps.instruction: Pour 10 mL 4 % agar in PBS (maintained at 40–45 °C) into a well of a 6‑well plate, submerge the brain, and keep on ice until the agar solidifies.

steps.title: Trim agar block
steps.instruction: Remove the solidified agar block, trim excess agar with a razor blade to a cuboid shape while keeping the brain centered.

steps.title: Mount agar block for slicing
steps.instruction: Glue the agar block to the bottom of a specimen tray with super‑glue, add 0.1 M PB (pH 7.4) to the bath.

steps.title: Section brain
steps.instruction: Cut 1‑mm thick slices with a vibratome, collect slices into 8 mL PBS in a 6‑well plate; slices can be stored in 0.02 % NaN₃/PBS at 4 °C for up to 4 weeks (wash before further use).

steps.title: Pre‑incubate slices in ScaleA2
steps.instruction: Place 2–3 slices into 8 mL pre‑warmed ScaleA2 solution (4 M urea, 10 % glycerol, 0.1 % Triton‑X‑100, 1 % v/v ddH₂O) in a 6‑well plate; incubate 24 h at 37 °C with shaking at 90 rpm.

steps.title: Wash after ScaleA2
steps.instruction: Wash slices twice with 8 mL PBS for 15 min each on a rotary shaker at 20–25 °C, 50–100 rpm.

steps.title: Quench endogenous peroxidase
steps.instruction: Incubate slices in 6 mL endogenous peroxidase quenching solution (1 % H₂O₂ in PBS) for 1 h on a rotary shaker at 20–25 °C, 50–100 rpm.

steps.title: Wash after quenching
steps.instruction: Wash slices twice with 8 mL PBS for 15 min each under the same shaking conditions.

steps.title: Incubate with POD‑nAb
steps.instruction: Transfer slices to 1,200 µL POD‑nAb solution (20 % culture supernatant, 0.3 % Triton‑X‑100 v/v, 0.02 % thimerosal) in a 2 mL safe‑lock tube; incubate 20–24 h at 20–25 °C with gentle rocking (50–100 rpm).

steps.title: Wash after POD‑nAb
steps.instruction: Wash slices four times with PBS‑X for 30 min each on a rotary shaker at 20–25 °C, 50–100 rpm.

steps.title: Wash with PB
steps.instruction: Wash slices three times with 0.1 M PB (pH 7.4) for 5 min each under the same shaking conditions.

steps.title: FT‑GO reaction
steps.instruction: Incubate slices in 1,200 µL FT‑GO reaction mixture (10 µM CF‑tyramide, 3 µg/mL GO solution, 2 % BSA in 0.1 M PB) for 4 h at 20–25 °C, 50–100 rpm.

steps.title: Add glucose to FT‑GO
steps.instruction: Add 12 µL β‑D‑glucose solution (200 mg/mL) to the reaction and incubate further 30–120 min at 20–25 °C, 50–100 rpm.

steps.title: Wash after FT‑GO
steps.instruction: Wash slices twice with PBS‑X for 15 min each on a rotary shaker at 20–25 °C, 50–100 rpm.

steps.title: Post‑fix slices
steps.instruction: Incubate slices in 6 mL fixative solution (4 % PFA in 0.1 M PB) for 20–24 h at 4 °C with gentle rocking (50–100 rpm).

steps.title: Final PBS wash
steps.instruction: Wash slices twice with 8 mL PBS for 15 min each on a rotary shaker at 20–25 °C, 50–100 rpm.

steps.title: Clear slices in ScaleS4
steps.instruction: Place slices into 8 mL pre‑warmed ScaleS4 solution (4 M urea, 40 % D‑sorbitol, 10 % glycerol, 0.2 % Triton‑X‑100, 25 % DMSO) and incubate 12–16 h at 37 °C with shaking at 90 rpm until transparent.

steps.title: Mount cleared slice
steps.instruction: Place the cleared slice on the bottom coverslip of a 3‑D‑printed imaging chamber.

steps.title: Remove excess ScaleS4
steps.instruction: Wipe away residual ScaleS4 solution surrounding the slice.

steps.title: Add ScaleS4 gel
steps.instruction: Drop 600–800 µL ScaleS4 gel (1.5 % agarose in ScaleS4 D25(0) solution) onto the slice to fill the chamber.

steps.title: Seal imaging chamber
steps.instruction: Place a coverslip over the gel, add a piece of Kimwipe on the coverslip, then lay a glass slide on top.

steps.title: Gel solidify
steps.instruction: Transfer the chamber to a 4 °C refrigerator, place metal weights on the slide, and let the gel solidify for 30–60 min.

steps.title: Finalize chamber assembly
steps.instruction: Remove weights, slide, and Kimwipe; wipe excess gel; attach the chamber to the bottom of a 60‑mm glass petri dish using Blu‑Tack at multiple points.

steps.title: Equilibrate chamber in ScaleS4
steps.instruction: Add ScaleS4 solution to the dish, incubate 30–60 min, then replace with fresh ScaleS4 solution.

steps.title: Set objective correction collar
steps.instruction: Adjust the correction collar of the 16× multi‑immersion objective lens to a refractive index of 1.47.

steps.title: Mount and focus on sample
steps.instruction: Place the petri dish on the microscope stage, immerse the objective in ScaleS4 solution, approach the cleared slice while removing any air bubbles from the lens tip.

steps.title: Configure imaging parameters
steps.instruction: Set laser power, scan speed, pinhole size (1.0 Airy unit), detector gain, amplifier offset, xy and z resolution, and bit depth; enable z‑compensation so laser intensity/detection gain increase with depth.

steps.title: Acquire CLSM images
steps.instruction: Collect confocal laser‑scanning microscopy images of the cleared slice and save the files.

steps.title: Process images
steps.instruction: Process the acquired images using LAS‑X and/or Fiji software.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol or parts of it have been used and validated in the following research article: • Yamauchi et al. [14]. A three dimensional immunolabeling method with peroxidase-fused nanobodies and fluorochromized tyramide-glucose oxidase signal amplification. Commun Biol (Figures 1c, 5b–c, and 8c–d, and Supplementary Movies 1 and 3). We provide validation data in Figure 3, which shows an example of GFP POD-nAb/FT-GO 3D-IHC in the cerebral cortex of a 1-mm-thick brain slice infected with AAV2/PHP.eB CAG EGFP WPRE (n = 3 slices from 3 mice). xy images obtained at depths of 100, 500, and 900 μm are represented in each panel (Figure 3A–C). Neuronal and glial processes in a 1-mm-thick mouse brain slice are stained with a high signal/noise ratio by POD-nAb/FT-GO 3D-IHC for GFP. The staining procedure of GFP POD-nAb/3D-IHC can be completed within three days. POD-nAb/FT-GO 3D-IHC allows for highly sensitive detection of target molecules in mouse brain tissues. We have shown that POD-nAb/FT-GO for GFP yields 9.0- and 6.8-fold signal amplification compared with EGFP fluorescence and conventional 3D-IHC using a synthetic fluorophore-conjugated anti-GFP nAb, respectively [14]. Figure 3. GFP POD-nAb/FT-GO 3D-IHC in a 1-mm-thick mouse brain slice. (A–C) xy images at depths of 100, 500, and 900 μm in a 1-mm-thick brain slice stained by POD-nAb/FT-GO 3D-IHC for GFP. The brain slice is prepared from a mouse infected with AAV2/PHP.eB CAG-EGFP-WPRE. The images are acquired with z-compensation to compensate for depth-dependent signal loss. The pinhole size is set to 1.0 Airy unit during imaging acquisition. Scale bar: 50 μm. POD-nAb, peroxidase-fused nanobody; FT-GO, fluorochromized tyramide-glucose oxidase; 3D-IHC, three-dimensional immunohistochemistry; GFP, green fluorescent protein.
